page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. This server features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports hardware-level features such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES cryptography, and SHA-NI instructions. This instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate a clear performance asymmetry. The server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng testing, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores, fall into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is also constrained, with Passmark memory scores and small-block read-only memory bandwidth categorized as poor (bottom 10%). Large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidths perform in the average range at 43.63 GB/sec and 30.48 GB/sec, respectively. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average throughput, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is poor.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-highcpu-4 offers a dedicated CPU allocation with a highly constrained memory profile, making it a specialized option where raw compute threads are prioritized over memory capacity. Due to the 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, this server is poorly suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale compilation, or complex multi-threaded operations. It is best utilized for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks, basic text processing, or low-intensity web serving where high memory density is not required.
